title: A non-canonical JAK/STAT pathway promotes viral replication through the lipoprotein receptor-related protein in ticks
experiments_summary: The study employed a combination of in vivo tick infection models, cell-based assays, transcriptomics, lipidomics, and biochemical methods. (1) Gene expression profiling: RT-qPCR was used to measure expression of JAK/STAT components (Dome, STAT) and LRP in Haemaphysalis longicornis nymphs at two days post-feeding on LGTV-infected mice. (2) RNAi-mediated gene knockdown in ticks: dsRNA targeting Dome, STAT, LRP, LC3, and GFP (control) was microinjected into tick nymphs via the anal pore; knockdown efficiency was verified by RT-qPCR. LGTV infection was introduced either by microinjection (300 PFU) or by allowing ticks to feed on LGTV-infected interferon receptor-deficient A6 mice; viral loads were quantified by RT-qPCR targeting the preM gene at days 6 and 10. (3) ISE6 cell knockdown: Dome and STAT were silenced in Ixodes scapularis ISE6 cells using lipofectamine-mediated dsRNA transfection, followed by LGTV infection at MOI=0.1, with viral load assessed by RT-qPCR. (4) Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays: HEK-293T cells were co-transfected with Flag-tagged STAT and HA-tagged individual LGTV NS proteins (NS1–NS5) to test for STAT–NS protein interactions; LRP-Flag and NS5-HA (LGTV and TBEV) were co-transfected to assess LRP–NS5 interactions; LRP-Flag and LGTV E-HA were co-transfected to test LRP–E protein interaction. Immunoprecipitation used anti-Flag or anti-HA beads and western blotting. (5) LRP overexpression in BHK-21 cells: LRP-Flag was transfected into BHK-21 cells, which were then infected with LGTV (MOI=1); preM mRNA and E protein levels were measured by RT-qPCR and western blot. (6) Viral entry and binding assays: LRP-overexpressing BHK-21 cells were incubated with LGTV (MOI=10) at 4°C for binding or at 37°C for internalization; viral RNA was quantified post-wash by RT-qPCR. (7) LGTV replicon assay: BHK-21 cells were transfected with LRP, then transfected with an LGTV replicon lacking structural genes; NS5 mRNA was measured to assess replication. (8) Confocal immunofluorescence microscopy: Subcellular localization of LRP and NS5 or E protein was examined in BHK-21 cells using anti-HA and anti-Flag antibodies; co-localization was quantified using Pearson's coefficient in ImageJ. Tick midguts were also examined for dsRNA (J2 antibody) and LDs co-localization. (9) RNA sequencing (transcriptomics): dsGFP- and dsSTAT-treated nymphs (four biological replicates, 10 ticks per replicate) were collected after two days of feeding; RNA was extracted and sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq platform; differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq with adjusted P<0.05 and |log2 fold change|>1. (10) Lipid droplet (LD) analysis: Tick midguts from dsLRP or dsGFP nymphs, and LGTV-infected or uninfected nymphs, were stained with BODIPY 493/503 and imaged by confocal microscopy; mean fluorescence intensity was quantified with ImageJ. (11) Non-targeted lipidomics: Midguts from dsLRP- and dsGFP-treated nymphs (5 biological replicates, 60 midguts each) were analyzed by LC-MS/MS; data were processed with Progenesis QI and lipids identified against the LipidMaps database. (12) ATP quantification: Midguts from knockdown or LGTV-infected nymphs (6 replicates, 10 midguts each) were homogenized and ATP was measured using an Enhanced ATP Assay Kit with luminescence detection. (13) Autophagy assessment: LC3 protein levels in tick lysates were measured by western blot using anti-LC3B antibody following dsLRP knockdown, LGTV infection, or rapamycin treatment (500 nM, 20 nL microinjected); lysosome abundance was assessed by LysoTracker Deep Red staining of midguts; LC3 knockdown was performed to examine its effect on LDs and viral load. (14) Rapamycin treatment: Nymphs were microinjected with rapamycin (500 nM, 20 nL) to activate autophagy, and LC3 levels and LD abundance were subsequently assessed. (15) LRP–NS5 co-expression experiment: BHK-21 cells were co-transfected with LRP-Flag and NS5-HA at a 2:1 mass ratio, and LC3 levels were measured by western blot to assess autophagy induction. (16) Structural domain analysis: SMART (Simple Modular Architecture Research Tool) was used to compare domain architecture of H. longicornis LRP with human LDLR and LRP homologs from other tick species. All statistical analyses used GraphPad Prism 8.0 with unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test or one-way ANOVA.
